questions.question: Xu’s notification formats in scope are:
options: Only carrier pigeons and fax machines in real production systems at scale.
Mobile push, SMS, and email.
Only in-process log lines with no user delivery.
Only browser localStorage writes on the same device.
questions.explanation: mobile push notification, SMS message, and Email

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: mobile push notification, SMS message, and Email

questions.question: iOS push delivery commonly goes through:
options: A random public MQTT broker with no auth in real production systems at scale.
Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) using device token + payload.
Direct SMS gateways that ignore device tokens in real production systems at scale.
FTP uploads to each phone overnight in real production systems at scale.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide

questions.question: Android push in Xu’s overview commonly uses:
options: APNS exclusively for all Android devices in real production systems at scale.
Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) as a common path.
Only postal mail with printed QR codes in real production systems at scale.
Direct SQL inserts into the phone’s SQLite over the open internet.
questions.explanation: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) is commonly used

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) is commonly used

questions.question: Contact info gathering stores device tokens separately because:
options: A user can have multiple devices that should all receive pushes.
Device tokens must never be associated with a user id in real production systems at scale.
Email and SMS cannot be stored in any database table in real production systems at scale.
APNS forbids persisting tokens longer than one second in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: A user can have multiple devices

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: A user can have multiple devices

questions.question: True or false: Users who opt out should stop receiving notifications.
questions.explanation: users who choose to opt-out will no longer receive notifications

questions.question: Calling the system “soft real-time” means:
options: Messages may be delayed forever with no delivery goal in real production systems at scale.
Deliver ASAP, but slight delay under high load is acceptable.
Every notification must arrive within one microsecond worldwide.
Notifications only send when the on-call engineer presses a button.
questions.explanation: soft real-time… slight delay is acceptable
